0.text: The process starts by confirming the basic information. Following this, two streams of activities occur in parallel. In one stream, the process's components are identified. In the other stream, the process performance is assessed, and then it is confirmed if the process requires optimization. If optimization is not required, the process is completed. However, if optimization is required, the process waits for the identification of the process's components to be completed. Once both parallel streams are finished, the process continues by defining how long it takes to complete the process, after which the potential process improvements are written. Next, approval is sought for the processing improvements. After approval is granted, two more activities happen in parallel: the updated process is used, and simultaneously, it is defined what would make the improvements successful. Once both of these are done, the process changes are communicated and the next process review and optimization are scheduled, also in parallel. After the process changes are communicated, they are implemented, and the process is completed. The process also completes after the next process review and optimization is scheduled.

0.text: The process begins by recording the order details. Following this, two sets of actions occur in parallel. First, the system checks that the products are in stock, and then the ordered products are requested from the inventory. At the same time, a record is made of which products were taken from storage, and then quality checks are performed. Once both the products have been requested and the quality checks are complete, one or both of the following may happen: the items are packaged securely, and/or approval is obtained. If approval is obtained, three more actions occur simultaneously: the packing slip is printed, the products are measured, and the shipping label is attached to the packaging, which is then followed by printing the invoice. After all active paths are completed, the items are loaded into the delivery vehicle. Finally, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, and the process is completed.

One or both of the following paths can be taken. In one path, the items are packaged securely. In the other path, approval is obtained. After getting approval, three actions happen in parallel: the packing slip is printed, the products are measured, and the shipping label is attached to the packaging. After attaching the shipping label, the invoice is printed. Once the packing slip is printed, the products are measured, and the invoice is printed, the items are loaded into the delivery vehicle. A confirmation email is then sent to the customer. Finally, after the items are either packaged securely, or the confirmation email has been sent, or both, the process concludes.

0.text: The Accounts Receivable Process begins by recording the buyer's details. Following this, two activities occur in parallel: a credit application form is sent to the buyer, and a credit check is run on the purchasing company. After the credit application form is sent, approval is sought for a post-credit check review, and simultaneously, the buyer is sent the terms of sale. Once the credit check is complete, the approval has been given, and the terms of sale have been sent, the process continues. At this point, one or both of the following may happen: the customer payment terms are checked, and the invoice is sent using the accounting software. After these invoicing actions are completed, one or more follow-up actions are taken, which can include recording the activity digitally, establishing monthly contact with the client, and making a second physical copy. Subsequently, the sales are recorded, which may involve recording the sales on credit of goods, recording the sales on credit of services, or both. Once all selected sales recording activities are finished, the process is completed.

After all ticket type determinations are complete, the process continues. It may involve replicating the issue, after which the process ends. Alternatively, or in addition, the ticket question is responded to, followed by testing technical issues, which then concludes the process.

Once the application is completed, it is sent to the Lender. The Lender then simultaneously gives a written notice to the applicant, sends the application back to the applicant, and checks for completeness. After all these actions are finished, the Lender begins the underwriting process. This leads to three parallel outcomes: the loan amount is reduced, the loan application is approved, and the interest rate is changed. Once these underwriting decisions are finalized, the outcome is communicated to the Borrower, who then receives the loan funds, and the process ends.

0.text: The process starts by setting the target date for approval. Following this, two tasks are performed in parallel: reviewing the most recent budget and evaluating any significant variances. Once both are complete, the ways of achieving the goals are determined. Next, the total annual budget is calculated at the same time as the average monthly cost is estimated. After both of these tasks are finished, the total annual income is projected. Then, in parallel, the financial data is recorded in a budget spreadsheet while the budget is finalized. After these steps, a decision is made. One or both of the following paths can be taken. In one path, approval is requested from top management. In the other path, management responsibilities are assigned, which is followed by two parallel tasks: obtaining approval from top management and incorporating the budget into the master budget. Once all active paths are completed, the process concludes with the status "Completed".

0.text: The process begins with sending to the vendor accounting department, after which a receiving report is created. Following this, two actions occur in parallel: the vendor's invoice is gathered, and a three-way match is double-checked. After the double-check, the receiving report is gathered and, at the same time, errors are reported to the relevant team member. Once the vendor's invoice is gathered, the receiving report is gathered, and errors have been reported, three more actions happen concurrently: dates are checked to avoid penalty charges, the information is stored in the paid invoice file, and the invoice is entered into the accounts payable account. After checking the dates, a voucher is created for the documents and all documents are stamped in parallel. The process then waits for the storing in the paid invoice file, the entering of the invoice into the accounts payable account, and the stamping of all documents to be complete. Finally, after the voucher has also been created, the payment is scheduled, and the process is completed.

0.text: The process begins by recording the customer's basic details. Following this, three activities occur in parallel: ways to increase value are determined, key points of value are identified, and an analysis of how they use the product is conducted, which is then followed by quantifying the impact of cancellation. Once all these preparatory steps are completed, the process continues by simultaneously confirming the call date and time and giving the customer a call. After the call date and time are confirmed, one or both of the following may happen: a record is made of whether or not the customer responded, which leads to sending them an email, and a record is made of their willingness to talk. The process waits for these actions and the call itself to be completed. Subsequently, one or both of the following actions may take place: summarizing why they want to leave and asking open-ended questions. After these are done, three more actions happen in parallel: ideas to increase value are described, they are presented with a special offer, and they are informed of key metrics demonstrating value. Once these are all complete, one or both of the following may occur: they are thanked for their time and feedback, and the customer's decision is recorded. Finally, the process concludes by asking if they have any other concerns and then noting down important learnings from the conversation, at which point the process ends.

0.text: The process starts with recording basic details. After this, two activities occur in parallel: the most recent budget is reviewed, and any significant variances are evaluated. Once both are complete, the process continues by prioritizing three to five goals and defining three to five goals, which also happen in parallel. Following the completion of these goal-setting activities, the next phase begins. In one parallel path, the average monthly cost is estimated. Simultaneously, in another path, the total annual budget is calculated, which is then followed by listing all department expenses. After all these financial estimations are done, the total annual income is projected. Subsequently, the financial data is recorded in a budget spreadsheet at the same time as the budget is finalized. Finally, in the last parallel stage, the budget is incorporated into the master budget, while at the same time, management responsibilities are assigned, and then approval is requested from top management. Once all these final activities are finished, the process concludes as completed.

0.text: The process starts when a Borrower submits their ID proof. Following this, two things happen in parallel: the Borrower completes the loan application, while the Lender's Credit Department receives the application along with the submitted ID proof. Once both of these actions are finished, the Credit Department checks the application for completeness. If the application is found to be incomplete, a written notice is sent to the Borrower. If the application is complete, the process moves forward. At this point, the Credit Department begins two more parallel actions: they begin the underwriting process and simultaneously check the applicant's credit score and risk score. After the root cause identification, the call, and recording their willingness to talk are all complete, ideas to increase value are described. Then, in parallel, the customer's decision is recorded and they are thanked for their time and feedback. Once both actions are complete, they are asked if they have any other concerns. Finally, two last actions happen in parallel: important learnings from the conversation are noted down, and these learnings are sent to the appropriate managers. After both are finished, the process concludes.

After this, two actions occur in parallel: a written notice is given to the applicant, and the application is checked for completeness. Following the written notice, the application is sent back to the applicant. Once the application has been sent back and the completeness check is finished, the underwriting process begins. Subsequently, three actions happen at the same time: the interest rate is changed, the loan application is approved, and the loan amount is reduced. After all three of these actions are completed, the user receives the loan funds, and the process is completed.

0.text: The process is initiated by the Borrower, who provides a bank statement to the Lender. The Lender's Credit Department receives the application. Following this, a message is sent to the Borrower to complete the loan application. Simultaneously, the Credit Department sends the application back to the applicant and gives written notice to the applicant in parallel. After these actions, the Credit Department may begin the underwriting process, check the credit score and risk score, or perform both actions. Subsequently, the Credit Department may decide to change the interest rate, reduce the loan amount, or do both. Depending on the outcome, a message is sent to the Borrower, who then receives the loan funds, at which point the process concludes.

0.text: The Budget Process begins when the Budget Preparer sets the target date for approval. Following this, two activities occur in parallel: any significant variances are evaluated, and the most recent budget is reviewed. Once both of these are complete, the Budget Preparer prioritizes three to five goals and then estimates the average monthly cost. Next, in another set of parallel activities, all sources of income are listed, and the total annual income is projected. After both of these actions are finished, the Budget Preparer records the financial data in a budget spreadsheet. The spreadsheet is then passed to Top Management, who obtains approval, and the process comes to an end.

0.text: The process starts by recording basic details and then identifying the key points of value. Following this, three actions are initiated in parallel: an email is sent to them, the call date and time are confirmed, and it is recorded if they are willing to talk. After the email is sent, two more parallel actions occur: it is recorded whether or not the customer responded, and they are given a call. Once both of these are completed, the next set of parallel activities begins, which involves asking open-ended questions, summarizing why they want to leave, and identifying the root cause(s) of the problem. After these three actions are finished, they are informed of key metrics demonstrating value and are presented with a special offer, both happening in parallel. Subsequently, they are thanked for their time and feedback, and the customer's decision is recorded, again in parallel. Finally, after these are done, it is asked if they have any other concerns, the learnings are sent to the appropriate managers, and the process concludes.

0.text: The process begins when one wants to learn how to identify future failures. The first step involves three concurrent activities: specificking the product market share, checking the location of the startup, and doing the SWOT analysis. While the product market share is being specified and the SWOT analysis is being done, the location of the startup is checked, which is then followed by making plans for future products. Once all three initial streams are complete, one or more of the following reviews can be performed: reviewing the number of employees, reviewing the business plan, or reviewing the company mission and direction. If the number of employees is reviewed, this is followed by reviewing enthusiasm. If the business plan is reviewed, the process moves on. If the company mission and direction are reviewed, two parallel activities begin: reviewing trustworthiness and reviewing the ability as a team leader. While the ability as a team leader is being reviewed, the trustworthiness review is followed by an optional review of team chemistry and/or expertise. After these team aspects are reviewed and the ability as a team leader review is complete, one or more financial checks can be performed: checking the exit strategy and/or checking the cash flow. Following these financial checks, two concurrent competition analyses are conducted: analyzing the reputation of the competition and knowing the exact competition. Once all active review paths have converged, the trademarks are checked, and the process concludes with the process being completed.

One or both of the following may occur: calculating the grades or applying special grades to individuals. If the grades are calculated, this is followed by two parallel actions: preparing the grades for SSO and selecting the exam assignment. Once both are complete, two more parallel actions occur: applying any changes and reviewing the course summary. After applying changes, the grades summary is reviewed. The process then continues after the review of the course summary, the review of the grades summary, and the application of special grades to individuals are all complete. At this point, three parallel actions take place: exporting the final grades, recalculating the grades, and exporting the course summary. Once all three actions are finished, the process concludes with two final parallel steps: sending the examiners a grade approval sheet and submitting the results to the SSO. The process ends when both of these final steps are completed.

The second involves updating the project management profile and then researching the campaign ideas. The third is scheduling future calls. Once all these parallel activities are completed, the client is informed of the project start. Following this, one or both of the following paths can be taken: either changes are made based on a follow-up call, or a post-onboarding survey is sent, which is then followed by having a follow-up call. After all selected paths are finished, the process is completed.

Creating first draft of the marketing plan
Get approval for the first draft
Making changes based on follow-up call

2.text: The process begins with an onboarding call with the client. Following this call, three streams of work commence in parallel. In the first stream, a first draft of the marketing plan is created, and then approval is sought for this draft. Simultaneously, in the second stream, the project management profile is updated, which is followed by research into campaign ideas. In the third parallel stream, future calls are scheduled. Once approval for the first draft is obtained, the campaign ideas have been researched, and future calls have been scheduled, the client is informed of the project start. After this, one or both of the following actions can occur: changes are made based on a follow-up call, or a post-onboarding survey is sent, which then leads to a follow-up call. After all selected actions are completed, the process concludes as completed.

0.text: The process begins with the start of onboarding. First, an introduction is made. Following this, two activities occur simultaneously: a job description with responsibilities is provided, and the employee's workstation is prepared. Once both of these are complete, a series of activities are initiated in parallel. These activities include assigning a mentor, taking the new employee out to lunch, getting approval, assigning their first project, and encouraging them to socially interact with the team. Concurrently, reading material for personal growth is provided, which is then followed by a review of the onboarding process over the next 60 days. After all these parallel activities have been completed, the process concludes and is marked as completed.

tasks.name: Provide a job description with responsibilities
Encouraging them to socially interact with the team
Providing reading material for personal growth
Reviewing onboarding process over the next 60 days

0.text: The process begins by recording the buyer's details. Following this, three activities occur in parallel: approval is obtained for a post-credit check review, a credit check is run on the purchasing company, and the buyer is sent your terms of sale. Once all three of these activities are complete, the invoice is sent in your accounting software and, at the same time, the customer payment terms are checked. After both of these are done, the process continues with three more parallel activities: your activity is recorded digitally, a second physical copy is made manually, and monthly contact is established with your client. When all three of these actions are finished, the sales on credit of services are recorded in parallel with recording the sales on credit of goods. Once both sales are recorded, the process is completed.

0.text: The process begins by sending the item to the receiving department, after which a receiving report is created. Following this, three activities happen in parallel. Firstly, the vendor's invoice is gathered. Secondly, it is confirmed that all documents have been amended, which is followed by a double-check of a three-way match. Thirdly, any errors are reported to the relevant team member, and then the receiving report is gathered. Once all three parallel activities are completed, the dates are checked to avoid penalty charges, and the process concludes.

Following this, two actions occur in parallel: the Borrower completes the loan application, and the Credit Department receives the application. Once both actions are complete, the Credit Department may choose to send the application back to the applicant, give written notice to the applicant, or do both. 1.text: The process begins with the Borrower, who fills in an employment information form. Following this, two actions occur simultaneously: the Borrower completes the loan application, and the Bank's Credit Department prepares to receive the application. The Borrower sends the completed Loan Application to the Credit Department. After the application is both completed and received, the Credit Department may take one or more of the following actions: send the application back to the applicant or give a written notice to the applicant. Once these actions are complete, the Credit Department begins two parallel processes: it begins the underwriting process and it checks the credit score and risk score. After both underwriting has begun and the scores have been checked, the Credit Department proceeds with two more parallel actions: it approves the loan application, and it changes the interest rate, which is then followed by reducing the loan amount. Once these final decisions are made, the Bank sends the Loan Funds to the Borrower. The Borrower then receives the loan funds, and the process concludes.

If it is a 'Marketing/PR Question', then one or more of the subsequent steps are performed: either the ticket type is determined as a 'Feature Request', or it is determined as an 'I'm not sure question'. If it is an 'I'm not sure question', then at the same time, the ticket type is determined as an 'App Question' and as a 'Mixed-type question'. Once both of these are determined, this path converges with the 'Feature Request' path. After the 'Marketing/PR Question' path is complete, it joins with the 'Technical Issue' path. Following this, three actions are performed in parallel: replicating the issue, responsing to the ticket question, and testing technical issues. Once all three actions are complete, the process ends.

After all ticket types have been determined, three actions are performed in parallel: the issue is replicated, the ticket question is responded to, and technical issues are tested. Once all three of these actions are complete, the process ends.

0.text: The process starts with recording the basic details. After this, two actions occur in parallel: reviewing the most recent budget and evaluating any significant variances. Once both are complete, the process continues by simultaneously determining ways of achieving the goals and defining three to five goals, which are then prioritized. Following the completion of these parallel steps, all department expenses are listed while, at the same time, the average monthly cost is estimated. After both of these are done, the total annual income is projected. Subsequently, the financial data is recorded in a budget spreadsheet in parallel with finalizing the budget. Finally, approval is requested from top management at the same time as it is obtained from them. Once both actions are finished, the process concludes.

After both the vendor's invoice is gathered and the three-way match is double-checked, and after it has been confirmed that all documents have been amended, a selection of follow-up actions is made. 0.text: The process begins when a payment is received. The first step is confirming that the payment has been received. After confirmation, one or more of the following actions are initiated: performing quality checks, checking that the products are in stock, and recording which products were taken from storage. If the products are checked for stock, this is followed by requesting the ordered products from your inventory and then printing a packing slip. After the packing slip is printed, two tasks are performed in parallel: examining your other orders for delivery overlaps and loading items into the delivery vehicle. Once the other orders are examined, the delivery is arranged. The process waits until both the delivery is arranged and the items are loaded into the vehicle before proceeding. All the initial paths converge, and once all active tasks are completed, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, which concludes the process with its completion.

0.text: The process begins when the borrower provides their bank statement to the lender and completes the loan application. Following this, two things happen at the same time: a written notice is given to the applicant, and the application is sent back to the applicant. The returned application is then checked for completeness. If it is not all complete, it is checked again until it is. Once the application is complete and the written notice has been given, the process continues. Concurrently, the underwriting process begins, and the credit score and risk score are checked. After both of these are done, the loan amount is reduced and the interest rate is changed, also at the same time. Finally, after these adjustments are made, the borrower receives the loan funds, and the process ends.

0.text: The process begins with making an introduction. Following this, two parallel paths are initiated. In the first path, the basic idea is recorded. In the second path, the approval status is identified. Based on this, one or more of the following actions are taken: working out its value and getting approval. Once these actions are complete and the basic idea has been recorded, the process continues. Next, three activities occur in parallel: laying out a timeline, setting a budget, and drawing up a project plan which is then followed by stating the available resources. After all three parallel paths are finished, a kickoff meeting is held, and the KPIs are recorded. Subsequently, two final parallel activities take place. The first is to evaluate project outcomes and then terminate contractors. The second is to ensure the project is completed. Once both of these are done, the process comes to an end.
